implemented: Versioned marketcow.realtime.sparse-index.v1 contract with SHA-256 state binding.
Sparse entries bind first/last WAL cursor, segment id, byte offset and previous record SHA-256.
O(log n) nearest boundary lookup via partition_point, followed by mandatory authoritative WAL verification.
Atomic owner-only index replacement with file fsync, rename and directory fsync.
Missing or malformed derived index is rebuilt from the verified append-only WAL.
Index symlinks or unsafe file types/permissions are rejected instead of followed.
Index maintenance occurs only after the WAL batch sync barrier; an index persistence failure prevents memory publication and poisons the writer for deterministic restart.

covered: cursor 1 and cursor 1024 locate the correct indexed WAL batches
corrupt index content is rebuilt exactly from authoritative WAL
symlink index is rejected and target content is unchanged

preserved_failures: The first targeted test used a received-at fixture only 1000 ms after the base source timestamp; events 1001-1024 were correctly rejected as InvalidTimestamp. The fixture boundary was corrected to 10000 ms and the same gate passed.
The first full clippy run rejected a bool::then closure as unnecessary lazy evaluation. It was mechanically changed to then_some and the exact clippy command passed.
explicit_non_claims: The index is currently verified or rebuilt after a full authoritative WAL integrity scan, so startup is not yet independent of total WAL history.
No compaction, archival rewrite, writer handoff or production cutover is enabled.
Phase 6 and the overall migration remain incomplete.
